Berossus (Bērōssos), Babyloniaka — the Flood of Xisouthros (Greek tradition)

Berossus, priest of Bel at Babylon, wrote the Babyloniaka (c. 290–278 BC) for Antiochus I. Lost; the flood story survives via Alexander Polyhistor → (a) Eusebius' Chronicle (Greek lost; Armenian translation survives) and (b) George Syncellus, Ecloga chronographica (Greek, c. 800 AD, partly via Eusebius/Annianus). A shorter parallel version comes from Abydenus (via Eusebius Praep. Ev. IX 12 and Syncellus).

Fragment numbering: Müller FHG II, Berosus fr. 7 (Syncellus p. 30 ed. Paris; Euseb. Arm.) = Jacoby FGrH 680 F4 (a: Syncellus, b: Euseb. Arm.) = Verbrugghe–Wickersham pp. 49–50; Abydenus = FHG IV p. 280 fr. 1–3 = FGrH 685 F2–3.

  • Jacoby, FGrH III C 1 (1958), no. 680 — standard critical text; Brill (copyright). Brill's New Jacoby (BNJ 680, G. De Breucker, 2016, with English translation & commentary) — subscription only (Brill Online, institutional); search "BNJ 680 Berossos" at referenceworks.brill.com.
  • S. M. Burstein, The Babyloniaca of Berossus (SANE 1/5, Undena 1978) — English translation; in copyright, out of print (second-hand copies). archive.org: lending only, if at all.
  • G. P. Verbrugghe & J. M. Wickersham, Berossos and Manetho, Introduced and Translated (Univ. of Michigan Press 1996/2001) — English; in copyright (~US$ 35 pb).
  • J. Karst, Eusebius Werke V: Die Chronik aus dem Armenischen übersetzt (GCS 20, Leipzig 1911) — German translation of the Armenian Chronicle (the fullest version of the flood fragment). Full view at https://archive.org/details/chronikausdemarm00euse (PDF 23.8 MB). Not downloaded: Karst died 1962, so it is PD in the US (pre-1929) but still protected in life+70 countries (EU/Israel) until end-2032.
  • A. Schoene, Eusebi Chronicorum libri duo, vol. I (Berlin 1875) — Armenian rendered into Latin (Petermann) with Greek parallels; public domain; not located on archive.org in this search (try HathiTrust / Google Books / BSB "Eusebi chronicorum libri duo").
  • Syncellus, ed. W. Dindorf, CSHB (Bonn 1829) — PD Greek text of Syncellus; ed. A. A. Mosshammer (Teubner 1984; copyright) is the modern standard.
  • sacred-texts.com Cory's Ancient Fragments: https://sacred-texts.com/cla/af/ — blocked by Cloudflare to scripts on 2026-10-16 (the archive.org scan in Cory-1876/ has the same text).
  • Livius.org (J. Lendering) has an English Berossus page — see ../Livius/ if present.

Assessment

For a Hebrew translation of the Greek flood fragment, the base text should be FHG fr. 7 (Syncellus) as in DFHG (saved, clean polytonic Greek, with Müller's notes on variants of Scaliger and Eusebius), checked against Jacoby FGrH 680 F4 (restricted) where possible. The Armenian Eusebius version (Karst German, Müller's Latin) differs in details (e.g. boat 15 stadia long in Eus. vs 5 in Syncellus; "pedestrian journey"), which a translation should note.
